title: Velebit Dry-Stone: Running the Premužić Trail

bestPeriod.avoid: November–April — the Oltari–Zavižan forest road is snow-gated, Alan is unstaffed, and bura closes the coastal approach; late July–August is brutally dry with every cistern at its lowest.

accommodation.note: Krasno/Starigrad rooms €45–€75 pppn; Zavižan and Alan hut bunks €15–€25

food.note: Lika konoba mains €10–€16; hut meals €8–€12; carried food for three days

transport.note: Hire car for the week (essential), fuel, the Oltari–Zavižan gravel road

activities.note: Northern Velebit NP and Paklenica NP entries, Botanical Garden, one guided day

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — five running days of 12–22 km with up to 1,450 m of vertical on limestone, plus genuine self-sufficiency on water

gatewayAirport: ZAD Zadar — 55 min to Starigrad-Paklenica, 2 h 15 min to Krasno; RJK Rijeka 1 h 45 min to Senj; ZAG Zagreb 2 h 30 min to Krasno
summary: Velebit is a 145 km limestone wall standing between the Adriatic and the Lika plateau, and almost none of it holds water. That single fact shapes everything: the running is fast, pale, waterless and strangely engineered, because in 1930–33 the forestry engineer **Ante Premužić** cut a graded dry-stone path across the wildest section of the range — 57 km from Zavižan south to Baške Oštarije, laid so gently that a laden horse could walk it, threading between the Rožanski and Hajdučki kukovi towers without ever needing a hand. This week runs the northern half of that path properly, adds the botanical high ground around Zavižan, drops to Paklenica for the canyon and the Vaganski vrh ridge, and builds in one genuine rest day on the coast. It suits self-sufficient runners who are comfortable carrying two litres and reading a limestone landscape with no streams in it.

itinerary.title: Zadar in, up the Lika side to Krasno
itinerary.morning: Land at ZAD, collect a car, and drive north — the coastal Adriatic road to Senj, then inland over to **Krasno**, Croatia's highest village and the Northern Velebit NP headquarters. Buy park tickets and the 1:30,000 map at **Kuća Velebita**.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy legs-opener on the forest tracks around Krasno at 700 m — nothing technical, just an hour of soft ground to shake off the flight and check the shoes against the first limestone.
itinerary.evening: Lika cooking in Krasno: lamb, cheese from the plateau, and *škripavac*. Buy three days of trail food here; the shop options above 1,000 m are none.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 180 m D+ / T1 / 50 min–1 h; drive 2 h 15; NP entry ≈€10

itinerary.title: Up the gravel to Zavižan, the botanical high ground
itinerary.morning: Drive the **Oltari–Zavižan forest road** — roughly 15 km of gravel with a barrier, slow and rough but manageable in a normal hire car when dry. Arrive at **Planinarski dom Zavižan (1,594 m)**, beside the highest permanently staffed meteorological station in Croatia.
itinerary.afternoon: Run the acclimatiser loop over **Veliki Zavižan** and **Vučjak** through the **Velebit Botanical Garden**, a 1967 reserve set in a limestone sinkhole holding the endemic Velebit degenia. Short, sharp and 1,600 m high.
itinerary.evening: Dinner and a bunk in the hut. Twenty-eight beds, a wood stove, and the whole Kvarner archipelago below you at sunset.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.2 km / 310 m D+ / T2 / 50 min–1 h 15; hut 1,594 m; carry 1.5 L

itinerary.title: Premužićeva staza to Rossijeva koliba and back
itinerary.morning: Onto the dry-stone path itself. Within two kilometres the trail enters the **Rožanski kukovi**, a strict reserve of limestone towers where leaving the marked path is forbidden — and the path threads it at a runnable grade the whole way.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn at **Rossijeva koliba**, an emergency shelter about two hours' walk from Zavižan and roughly the halfway feel of the northern section. Return the same way; the surface rewards a faster second half.
itinerary.evening: Back at Zavižan. Log the next day's route in the hut book — it is the only meaningful safety net up here.
itinerary.dayStats: 12.4 km / 380 m D+ / T1–T2 / 1 h 20–1 h 50 / ≈70% dry-stone path; no water on route

itinerary.title: The full northern Premužić section to Alan
itinerary.morning: Run the whole northern section south to **Planinarski dom Alan (≈1,340 m)** — 16.5 km of continuous engineered path, past the Hajdučki kukovi and above the Lubenovac basin, dropping steadily toward the Alan saddle.
itinerary.afternoon: Add the **Lubenovac circuit** from Alan if legs are fresh: sinkhole pasture, roofless shepherd huts and a silence that is genuinely total. Otherwise recover; the hut is basic, self-catering, and has no electric lighting.
itinerary.evening: Cook at Alan or eat what the warden is serving. Confirm your descent transport — this is a point-to-point day and the car is still at Zavižan.
itinerary.dayStats: 16.5 km / 560 m D+ / 810 m D− / T2 / 2 h–2 h 50 (+11 km, 420 m if adding Lubenovac); carry 2 L
itinerary.sleep: Planinarski dom Alan, or drive down to Starigrad-Paklenica

itinerary.title: Recovery on the coast: Zrmanja and sea
itinerary.morning: Down to **Starigrad-Paklenica**. Swim. The Adriatic here is clear and cold enough to work as an ice bath on tired quads.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to the **Zrmanja canyon** rim near Obrovac and walk or jog the easy rim path — 6 km, no vertical worth naming, and the green river 200 m below in a limestone slot.
itinerary.evening: Fish and *šparoge* in Starigrad, on a terrace, with the Velebit wall going pink behind you. Rehydrate deliberately: you have been running on cistern rations for three days.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km / 120 m D+ / T1 / 35–50 min; drive Alan→Starigrad ≈1 h 20

itinerary.title: Velika Paklenica: Anića kuk and Manita peć
itinerary.morning: Enter **Paklenica NP** at the Velika Paklenica gate and run up the canyon floor beneath **Anića kuk**, the 350 m limestone face that is the Balkans' most important big wall. Look up: on any dry morning there are climbers on it.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb the cabled rock steps to **Manita peć**, the show cave open on a restricted schedule, then loop via **Lugarnica** forest hut and the **Planinarski dom Paklenica** at 480 m before descending.
itinerary.evening: Konoba dinner in Starigrad. Sleep early — tomorrow starts before light.
itinerary.dayStats: 13.2 km / 720 m D+ / T2–T3 / 1 h 45–2 h 30; Paklenica NP entry ≈€10; Manita peć limited opening days

itinerary.title: Struge and Vaganski vrh, 1,757 m
itinerary.morning: From the Paklenica dom, take the long climb through beech to the **Struge** shelter at ≈1,400 m — the last water on the mountain, and it may not be there. Fill at Struge if the cistern holds; if not, turn the day around.
itinerary.afternoon: The ridge to **Vaganski vrh (1,757 m)**, Velebit's summit, with the Adriatic on one side and the Lika plateau on the other. Loose karst, real exposure to the seaward wind, T3 running. Descend by the ascent route — do not improvise a new line down this face.
itinerary.evening: Down, wash, and drive to Zadar. Last dinner in the old town inside the Roman forum walls.
itinerary.dayStats: 22 km / 1,450 m D+ / T3 on the ridge / 3 h 30–4 h 45; carry 2.5–3 L; summit 1,757 m
itinerary.sleep: Zadar, or out on a late flight

accommodationStrategy.name: Planinarski dom Zavižan
accommodationStrategy.description: Twenty-eight beds across small rooms and a dormitory, open **year-round**, with electricity and a telephone — genuinely unusual at this altitude in Croatia. It is the only sane base for the Premužić days, saving 90 minutes of gravel driving each way. The cistern is small: bring your own water for running and buy drinks from the warden rather than draining the supply. Bunk roughly €15–€25.

accommodationStrategy.name: Planinarski dom Alan
accommodationStrategy.description: Forty beds, a wooden cabin with a kitchen, **no electric lighting**, staffed daily from the end of May to the end of October and typically only on Sundays outside that. It is the natural end of the northern Premužić section and the gateway to Lubenovac. Bring a headtorch, food and a sleeping bag liner. The nearby Shepherds' Huts Alan sleep 24 from 1 May to 31 October with wood stoves and solar power, but their rainwater cistern is **not potable**.

accommodationStrategy.name: Seafront room in Starigrad-Paklenica
accommodationStrategy.location: coastal base for the southern half
accommodationStrategy.description: Two minutes from the Paklenica NP gate, so the Vaganski day starts without a drive, and directly on the water for post-run recovery. Rooms €45–€75 per night; most have a terrace, secure shoe-drying space and parking. Choose one on the north side of town to shorten the park approach.

logistics.connectivity: Croatia is inside EU roaming, so no surcharge. Signal is usable on seaward ridges and in Starigrad, **absent in Lubenovac, Šugarska duliba, the Rožanski towers and much of the Velika Paklenica floor**, and intermittent on the Oltari–Zavižan road. Offline maps are mandatory, not advisable.
logistics.emergency: **112** reaches **HGSS** (Hrvatska gorska služba spašavanja), the Croatian Mountain Rescue Service, whose Karlobag, Gospić and Zadar stations cover Velebit. Response to the Rožanski kukovi or the Vaganski ridge is measured in hours, not minutes. Croatia is in the EU and Schengen, so **EHIC/GHIC covers state treatment**, but helicopter extraction and repatriation are not covered — carry sports insurance that names mountain running.
logistics.weather: The **bura** is the headline: a cold, gusting, katabatic north-easterly that accelerates over the Velebit crest and hits the coast in violent bursts, closing the Maslenica bridge and the coastal road to high-sided vehicles. It can arrive in clear blue conditions. Summer afternoon thunderstorms build over the ridge from about 14:00. Temperature swing between Starigrad and Zavižan is routinely 12–15 °C.
logistics.bookingWindows: Zavižan and Alan bunks should be reserved through the huts or HPS **2–4 weeks ahead for June and September weekends**; midweek is usually walk-in-able but never assume. Manita peć runs on a **restricted opening schedule** — check the Paklenica NP site before building Day 6 around it. Starigrad rooms: 4–6 weeks in shoulder season, months in July–August.
logistics.money: Croatia uses the **euro** (since 2023). Cards work in Krasno, Starigrad and Zadar. **The mountain huts are cash** — carry €80–€120 in small notes for bunks, meals and water.
logistics.transportRules: A hire car is effectively mandatory; public transport does not reach Zavižan or Alan. Croatian motorway tolls are paid at barriers or by ENC transponder; the coastal Adriatic road is toll-free. The **Oltari–Zavižan forest road is a barriered gravel road**, snow-closed roughly November–May and unpleasant in a low car after heavy rain — check the gate status with the NP before committing. Cross-border hire into Bosnia (relevant if you detour to the Una) needs written permission and a green card.
logistics.permits: **Northern Velebit NP** and **Paklenica NP** charge separate daily entries of roughly €10 in season, sold at the gates and online. The **Rožanski and Hajdučki kukovi are a strict reserve**: staying on the marked Premužić trail is a legal requirement, not a suggestion, and off-trail movement there is prohibited. Wild camping is banned in both parks; bivouacking is tolerated only at designated points. Drones need permission. Do not take limestone, plants or the endemic Degenia velebitica.
logistics.health: Tap water in Krasno and Starigrad is potable; **cistern water is not, unless the warden says so** — carry a filter or purification tablets. **Ticks** are abundant in the beech and pasture zones April–October and Croatia has tick-borne encephalitis in the Lika region; check nightly and consider vaccination. **Poskok** (nose-horned viper, *Vipera ammodytes*) is genuinely present and genuinely venomous on the sunny southern slopes and in Paklenica — do not put hands into unseen rock. Brown bear, wolf and lynx live in Northern Velebit; encounters are rare and avoidance is simply noise.

proTips: **Treat water as the route-planning variable, not distance.** Plan every Velebit day backwards from where you can fill. If Struge's cistern is dry — and in September it often is — the Vaganski route becomes a 3 L carry or it does not happen.
**Phone Zavižan or Alan the day before and ask two questions:** is the cistern holding, and what is the wind doing on the ridge. The wardens give a better forecast than any app.

**Run the Premužić trail northbound if you can arrange the shuttle.** Alan → Zavižan gives you the Kvarner islands ahead of you in the light for the whole second half, and the net ascent lands earlier when you are fresh.

**Book a Zavižan bunk to skip the gravel road twice a day.** The Oltari approach eats 45 minutes each way and punishes hire-car suspension. Sleeping up there converts two commutes into two extra runs.

**Time Manita peć to its published opening days.** It runs on a short seasonal schedule with fixed hours, and a wasted 400 m climb to a locked cave gate is a genuinely dispiriting way to spend a morning.
**On a bura day, go into the Velika Paklenica canyon.** The walls shelter the floor almost completely while the ridge above is unrunnable, and the canyon is a full day on its own.
**Buy the paper 1:30,000 Velebit sheet at Kuća Velebita in Krasno.** Phone batteries die at 5 °C on the ridge, and the junction signage assumes you know which basin you are in.
**Wear shoes with a rock plate and full-cover uppers.** The *škrape* fissures here are the sharpest limestone in the Dinarides and will open both a mesh upper and a shin inside one week.
**Do the Zrmanja rest day properly.** Six easy kilometres and a cold swim between the Alan and Vaganski efforts is the difference between finishing the week and limping it.

raw.Zavižan – Veliki Zavižan – Vučjak – Bota: 7.2 km, 310 m D+, **50 min–1 h 15**. The acclimatiser.
raw.Zavižan – Premužićeva staza – Rossijeva: 12.4 km, 380 m D+, **1 h 20–1 h 50**. The purest stretch of the dry-stone path, running past the flanks of the Rožanski kukovi.
raw.Zavižan → Alan, full northern Premužić s: 16.5 km, 560 m D+ / 810 m D−, **2 h–2 h 50**. Point-to-point; needs a car shuttle or a hut night at Alan.
raw.Alan – Lubenovac – Alan circuit: 11 km, 420 m D+, **1 h 15–1 h 45**. Sinkhole pasture and abandoned shepherd settlements.
raw.Planinarski dom Paklenica → Struge → Vag: 22 km, 1,450 m D+, **3 h 30–4 h 45**. The week's big day and Velebit's highest point.
raw.Starigrad seafront + Zrmanja canyon rim: 6 km, 120 m D+, **35–50 min**. Recovery pace only.
raw.Technicality, stated on the SAC hiking s: The Premužić trail itself is a remarkable **T1–T2** for its altitude: graded, dry-stone-walled, never exposed, runnable at pace even where the surrounding terrain is vertical. Zavižan's summit spurs and the Lubenovac circuit are **T2**. Manita peć and the Anića kuk approach are **T2–T3** on polished, cabled rock steps. The Struge–Vaganski vrh ridge is **T3**: loose karst, a section of rock steps and real exposure on the seaward side in wind. Nothing on this itinerary requires a rope; nothing above T3 is included.
raw.Terrain composition, week average: ≈35% engineered dry-stone path and rock steps (the Premužić signature — hand-laid, wide enough for two, superb running surface), ≈25% bare fluted karst and rubble, ≈20% beech and black-pine forest singletrack, ≈12% gravel forest road, ≈8% grass sinkhole pasture. Croatian karst here is *škrape* — knife-edged fissured limestone that destroys soft uppers and lacerates hands in a fall. Rock plate, reinforced toe box, light gloves.
raw.Exposure and waymarking: Balkan standard **red circle with a white centre dot**, plus wooden signposts with hiking times (halve them for running). The Premužić trail is signed at both ends and at every junction; the **Velebitski planinarski put (VPP)** long-distance route shares much of it. Exposure on the Premužić section is negligible even where the drop beside it is not — the dry-stone parapets are the point. Exposure on the Vaganski ridge is real.
raw.Water refill points and month-by-month r: Velebit is porous karst with essentially **no surface water above 500 m**. Everything is cisterns and snowmelt.
raw.Zavižan hut (1,594 m): staffed year-round, but on a **limited-capacity cistern**. Water is available to guests and is sold; do not plan on filling four bottles for free. Reliable all season with courtesy.
raw.Rossijeva koliba: an unstaffed emergency shelter only. **No water, ever.**
raw.Alan hut (≈1,340 m): cistern water; staffed daily **end of May to end of October**, off-season usually only Sundays. Outside that window assume nothing.
raw.Shepherds' huts, Alan (1 May–31 Oct): rainwater cistern explicitly **not potable** — treat or boil.
raw.Lubenovac: the old shepherd cisterns are unreliable and often fouled. Do not count on them in any month.
raw.Struge (≈1,400 m, Paklenica): cistern fed by snowmelt and rain. Usually good **May–June**, dropping through July, and **frequently low or empty in late August and September**. This is the failure point on the Vaganski day.
raw.Velika Paklenica stream: flows well **March–May**, reduces to pools by July, often **dry August–September**. **Lugarnica** forest refreshment hut operates broadly April–October in daylight.
raw.Reliable taps: Krasno village, Starigrad-Paklenica, the Paklenica NP entrance. Fill there, every day, without exception. **Carry 2 L minimum on any Velebit ridge day and 2.5–3 L on the Vaganski route.**
raw.GPX sources and phone blackspots: GPX from the Croatian Mountaineering Association (HPS) Velebit Hiking Trail pages, the Northern Velebit NP site, Wikiloc and Komoot; the printed 1:30,000 Velebit sheets sold at the **Kuća Velebita** visitor centre in Krasno remain the reference. **Coverage:** decent on seaward-facing ridges with line of sight to the coast and around Starigrad; **dead in the Lubenovac and Šugarska duliba bowls, in the Rožanski kukovi, and for long stretches of the Velika Paklenica canyon floor.** The Oltari–Zavižan forest road has intermittent signal at best. Carry a fully offline map and tell the hut your plan.
raw.Bura management: The Senj–Velebit channel produces Europe's most notorious katabatic wind. Gusts of 150–200 km/h are recorded at the Maslenica bridge, which closes to high-sided vehicles and sometimes entirely. **A bura day is not a ridge day.** Signs: crystalline visibility, a lenticular cap on the ridge, a hard-edged cloud roll spilling seaward. Move the day to the sheltered Paklenica canyon floor or the Lika-side forest. Check DHMZ (meteo.hr) and the Zavižan station reading, which is the best real-time proxy for the ridge.
raw.Recovery: Day 5 is a true rest day: sea, the Zrmanja, and nothing above 120 m of ascent.

sources.verified: Northern Velebit NP's own accommodation listing — Zavižan hut 28 beds and open year-round with a limited-capacity cistern; Alan hut 40 beds, self-catering kitchen, no electric lighting, staffed end of May–end of October and usually Sundays off-season, managed by Orienteering Club Sljeme Zagreb; Shepherds' Huts Alan 24 places, 1 May–31 October, rainwater cistern explicitly not potable; Shepherds' Huts Lubenovac currently not for rent; Rossijeva koliba as an emergency-only shelter roughly two hours from Zavižan on the Premužić trail. Croatia's euro adoption and EU/Schengen status.
sources.confidenceNotes: Re-verify before publishing — (1) current **park entry fees** for both Northern Velebit and Paklenica, which have been revised repeatedly since euro conversion and vary by season; (2) **hut bunk and meal prices**, which are indicative; (3) the **Oltari–Zavižan forest road gate status and opening dates**, which shift year to year with snowfall and logging; (4) **Manita peć opening days and hours**, which are set seasonally by Paklenica NP; (5) the **Struge cistern's condition**, which is the single most consequential and most volatile fact in this file — it should be checked with the Paklenica NP office in the week of travel; (6) route distances, vertical and SAC grades, which are compiled from published trail data and GPX tracks rather than surveyed, and the running times, which assume a mid-pack runner on dry rock; (7) whether Alan is staffed on the specific dates of travel outside the core season.
